name: When should I consider replacing my roof instead of just repairing it?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider replacing my roof instead of just repairing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deciding between roof repair and replacement depends on several factors. If your roof is old (typically over 20-25 years for asphalt shingles), has widespread damage, or shows signs of significant wear such as curling, missing, or brittle shingles, a replacement is often more cost-effective in the long run. Frequent leaks in multiple areas, significant structural damage, or an outdated roof system are also strong indicators for replacement. Minor, localized issues or a relatively new roof can usually be addressed with repairs.
acceptedAnswer.description: Consider roof replacement if your roof is old, has widespread damage, frequent leaks, or significant structural issues. Minor, localized problems can often be repaired.
